title: Huddle: Corner Window for Every Claude Code Session Launches
summary: Open-source tool Huddle displays all running Claude Code sessions in a persistent corner window. Now available on GitHub for multi-session monitoring.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Huddle is a new open-source desktop tool that displays all running Claude Code sessions in a persistent corner window.
- The utility helps developers monitor multiple AI coding sessions simultaneously without switching between windows or terminal tabs.
- Available now on GitHub, Huddle addresses a common workflow pain point for developers using Claude Code across multiple projects.


A new open-source tool called Huddle brings persistent session monitoring to Claude Code users. The utility displays all running Claude Code sessions in a compact corner window, addressing a common workflow challenge for developers juggling multiple AI-assisted coding projects simultaneously.


Developer suren19113 released Huddle on GitHub on November 23, 2026, aiming to solve the context-switching overhead that emerges when developers run Claude Code across multiple terminal windows or project directories. The tool provides a live dashboard of active sessions without requiring manual window management or terminal multiplexing.


## How Huddle Works


Huddle runs as a lightweight desktop application that automatically detects active Claude Code processes. The corner window displays key information for each session:


- Project name or directory path
- Current task or file being processed
- Session duration and token usage estimates
- Quick-launch shortcuts to bring each session to focus


The persistent window stays on top of other applications, letting developers monitor AI coding progress across projects without switching contexts. Users can customize the window position, size, and opacity to fit their workflow preferences.


## Multi-Session Workflow Benefits


For teams and solo developers working on multiple codebases, Huddle eliminates the need to remember which terminal tab or window holds which Claude Code session. The tool is particularly useful for developers running simultaneous sessions for frontend and backend work, testing different approaches to the same problem, or managing code generation across microservices architectures.


The GitHub repository includes installation instructions for macOS, Linux, and Windows. Early feedback on Hacker News highlights demand for features like session grouping, custom labels, and integration with VS Code workspaces.


## Release Date and Availability


Huddle was officially launched on November 23, 2026, and is immediately available as an open-source project on GitHub. The tool requires no API keys or cloud services, running entirely locally to monitor Claude Code processes on the developer's machine.


The project is licensed under MIT, allowing commercial use and modification. The developer encourages community contributions and has outlined a roadmap for future versions, including support for other AI coding assistants and cross-platform session syncing.


## What This Means


Huddle represents the growing ecosystem of third-party tools built around AI coding assistants like Claude Code. As developers integrate AI more deeply into their workflows, utilities that solve coordination and monitoring challenges will become increasingly valuable. For teams scaling AI-assisted development across multiple projects, session management tools like Huddle can reduce cognitive overhead and improve productivity by making invisible background processes visible at a glance.
